facts.text: La Grange began as the Chickasaw trading post 'Itey Uch La,' meaning 'Cluster of Pines,' and was later named after the Marquis de Lafayette’s estate.
In 1854, the La Grange Female College opened its 25‑room brick building, offering advanced education for young women under Professor David Bancroft Johnson.
During the Civil War, La Grange’s position on the Memphis‑Charleston Railroad made it a strategic outpost occupied by both Union and Confederate forces.
The La Grange Historic District, added to the National Register in 1974, houses more than 75 19th‑century Greek Revival homes and churches like Hancock Hall.
La Grange sits on a ridge 200 feet above the Wolf River, just one mile north of the river’s banks.
